finding.claim: wipe() calls requireRole(u, "OWNER") but discards its boolean return, so the OWNER role check never gates repo.wipe(tenant); any caller of wipe can destroy a tenant regardless of roles.
finding.source: Any caller of wipe(User u, String tenant) (e.g. POST /tenants/{t}/wipe per comment at src/Admin.java:24) with a User whose roles lack OWNER; tenant is also caller-controlled.

trace.note: wipe(User u, String tenant) entered with any User
requireRole(u, "OWNER") called as bare statement; boolean result discarded
requireRole returns u.roles().contains(role) and does not throw (documented at line 13)

finding.guards_checked: requireRole (src/Admin.java:14-16) returns a boolean and is ignored by wipe; no if/throw between lines 26 and 27. Sibling export() (src/Admin.java:31-34) uses checkRole, which throws SecurityException (src/Admin.java:18-22), so export is correctly gated. Not verified: router/HTTP layer, Repo implementation, and whether tenant is bound to the caller's tenant (User has no tenant field), since those files are not in the audited directory.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. requireRole (src/Admin.java:14-16) returns a boolean and is invoked as a bare statement at src/Admin.java:26, so its result is discarded. No if/throw sits between lines 26 and 27. The throwing variant checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22) is used only by export (src/Admin.java:32), not wipe.
verdict.reason: wipe() at src/Admin.java:26 discards the boolean from requireRole, so repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27 runs for any User regardless of roles, while export() at src/Admin.java:32 correctly uses the throwing checkRole. The one caveat is that the router at the POST /tenants/{t}/wipe endpoint and the tenant-to-caller binding are outside the audited directory, so reachability by a low-privilege authenticated user is inferred from the comment at line 24 rather than verified.
